英文梗概: Jimmy McGill struggles to earn a living as a public defender while caring for his brother Chuck, a brilliant lawyer who avoids electricity. Hoping to attract a wealthy client, Jimmy approaches the Kettlemans, who face an embezzlement investigation. He also challenges HHM over Chuck's place at the firm. A staged accident involving two skateboarders is supposed to generate business, but they target the wrong car. Jimmy follows them to a house and unexpectedly encounters Tuco Salamanca.

Jimmy tries to talk Tuco out of killing the skateboarders after their scam insults Tuco's grandmother. His improvised negotiation saves their lives, although they leave with broken legs. The experience introduces Jimmy to Nacho, who sees an opportunity in the Kettlemans' stolen money. Nacho proposes robbing the family and paying Jimmy for information. Jimmy refuses the offer, but his concern about what might happen draws him further into a dangerous situation.

The Kettlemans disappear, and Nacho becomes the main suspect. Jimmy agrees to represent him and learns that Nacho's presence near the house may expose a separate crime. Believing the family staged its own disappearance, Jimmy searches for them instead of accepting the kidnapping theory. He finds the Kettlemans camping near their home with the missing money. Meanwhile, Mike helps Jimmy think through the case, beginning an uneasy professional connection between them.

The Kettlemans offer Jimmy money to keep quiet, which he accepts as a supposed retainer. He uses it to copy Howard's appearance and advertise beside an HHM-like logo. The firm demands that the billboard come down. Jimmy then stages a dramatic rescue of a worker hanging from the sign, winning publicity and new enquiries. His success depends on manipulating the story, while Chuck remains unaware of how his brother obtained the attention.

Jimmy's publicity brings a series of unsuitable clients, from an eccentric would-be sovereign to an inventor with an unfortunate product. An elderly client's will points him toward elder law, where patience and personal attention may provide a viable practice. Chuck is taken to hospital after an encounter outside his home. Jimmy resists treating his brother as incapable of making decisions. The episode links Jimmy's growing business ambitions with his protective, complicated loyalty to Chuck.

Philadelphia detectives question Mike about the deaths of two police officers. With Jimmy's help, Mike obtains information about their investigation. He later tells his daughter-in-law Stacey the truth about his son Matty: corrupt colleagues killed him despite his reluctant participation in their scheme. Mike explains his own role in taking revenge. His confession reveals the guilt beneath his controlled manner and why providing for Stacey and Kaylee matters so much to him.

The Kettlemans reject a plea agreement and abandon Kim for Jimmy, threatening Kim's position at HHM. Jimmy discovers that their expectations are impossible to satisfy honestly. He recruits Mike to recover the stolen cash and ensures that it reaches the authorities, including the money Jimmy had accepted. Without the cash as leverage, the family must return to Kim and face the deal. Jimmy protects Kim's work but loses the money and prospects he briefly imagined.

While helping an elderly client, Jimmy notices suspicious charges at Sandpiper Crossing. He investigates the billing, retrieves shredded documents and discovers a possible pattern of financial exploitation. Chuck becomes absorbed in the legal work and helps develop a substantial case. Their collaboration gives Jimmy hope that they can finally work as equals. As the case grows beyond a solo practice, the need for resources creates a new question about who will control it.

The Sandpiper case is taken to HHM, but the firm will not hire Jimmy. He initially blames Howard, then discovers that Chuck has been blocking his career. Chuck admits that he does not trust Jimmy with the responsibilities of a lawyer. The revelation breaks their apparent partnership. In a parallel story, Mike protects a nervous pharmaceutical employee during a criminal transaction, demonstrating his practical competence and his ability to distinguish professional discipline from empty intimidation.

Hurt by Chuck's rejection, Jimmy returns to Cicero and reunites with Marco. They revive their old cons, briefly escaping Jimmy's disappointment through familiar routines. Marco dies during their final scam, leaving Jimmy with another personal loss. Back in Albuquerque, a promising opportunity with Davis & Main offers a conventional legal career. Jimmy weighs that path against the freedom and excitement of his former life, questioning whether following the rules has rewarded him.

Jimmy initially turns down Davis & Main and spends time enjoying the idea of leaving conventional legal work behind. He and Kim con a boastful businessman at a hotel, reminding them both of the appeal of performance and deception. Jimmy ultimately accepts the firm's offer. Meanwhile, Pryce dismisses Mike as his bodyguard and exposes himself to Nacho, who steals his baseball cards. An attempt to recover the collection threatens to attract police attention to Pryce's illegal dealings.

Jimmy settles into Davis & Main, where an expensive office and professional support come with expectations about his conduct. Mike asks him to help Pryce, whose report of stolen baseball cards has raised police suspicions. Jimmy invents an embarrassing explanation involving private videos to divert the detectives from the real crime. The story works, but Kim is disturbed when she learns what he did. His ingenuity solves an immediate problem while creating a deeper disagreement about professional ethics.

Jimmy approaches Sandpiper residents during a bus trip and finds an effective way to recruit clients. He then makes a television commercial and airs it without obtaining approval from the Davis & Main partners. The advertisement generates calls, but its success does not erase the breach of trust. Kim faces consequences at HHM because of her association with him. Separately, Mike considers a job involving Tuco and begins looking for a way to act without committing murder.

Jimmy faces discipline over the unauthorized commercial, while Kim is pushed into document review at HHM. His attempts to defend her risk making matters worse. Mike rejects Nacho's request to kill Tuco and develops a different plan: provoke Tuco into assaulting him in front of the police. The operation puts Tuco in custody and leaves Mike badly injured. Mike gets the result he wanted, but the Salamancas' influence means the conflict cannot end with the arrest.

A flashback shows how easily Jimmy charms Chuck's wife Rebecca, highlighting the tension between the brothers. In the present, Kim works relentlessly to bring Mesa Verde to HHM, hoping to restore her standing. Winning the client does not immediately free her from punishment. Hector pressures Mike to change his account of Tuco's arrest. Jimmy's effort to navigate office rules and Mike's negotiations both show how powerful people impose conditions on those beneath them.

Kim receives an offer from Schweikart & Cokely and considers what a different firm might mean for her future. Jimmy continues to test the limits of his position at Davis & Main. Mike faces escalating pressure from Hector, including a threat involving his family. He negotiates payment in exchange for changing his statement about Tuco. The apparent agreement protects his immediate interests, but Mike remains unwilling to accept the Salamancas' power over his life.

Jimmy wants to leave Davis & Main without losing his bonus, so he makes himself increasingly difficult to keep. His deliberately disruptive behaviour finally gets him fired. He proposes starting a practice with Kim, who prefers separate businesses sharing an office and expenses. The arrangement offers closeness without complete professional dependence. Mike changes his statement about Tuco while planning his own response to Hector. Both men seek independence through carefully calculated compromises.

Kim leaves HHM and secures Mesa Verde for her new practice, but Chuck and Howard persuade the bank to stay with their firm. While caring for Chuck, Jimmy alters numbers in the bank's documents to undermine his brother's work. Mike studies Hector's operations and prepares to disrupt a transport route. The episode contrasts careful professional presentations with hidden interference, as Jimmy's desire to help Kim leads him to commit a serious violation of trust.

Chuck's Mesa Verde application fails because of the altered address. He becomes convinced that Jimmy manipulated the documents, while Kim benefits from the bank's renewed interest. Jimmy pressures a copy-shop employee to support his version of events. Chuck investigates in person and collapses, forcing Jimmy to choose between concealment and helping him. Mike successfully robs a Salamanca truck, but learns that an innocent witness was killed afterward, changing his assessment of what the operation achieved.

Chuck recovers after his collapse and presents himself as unable to continue practising law. Worried about his brother, Jimmy admits to altering the Mesa Verde documents. Chuck has secretly recorded the confession, turning an act of reassurance into potential evidence. Meanwhile, Mike prepares to shoot Hector but is interrupted by a warning left on his car. The season ends with both men's plans checked by opponents who understand more than they expected.

Chuck preserves Jimmy's recorded confession and allows Ernesto to hear part of it, setting a further plan in motion. Jimmy and Kim adjust to running their separate practices from the same office. Mike investigates the warning that stopped his attack on Hector. He discovers a tracker hidden in his car's fuel cap, replaces it and uses the replacement process to follow the people monitoring him. His patient investigation begins to reveal an organized operation behind the interference.

Mike follows the tracking operation to Los Pollos Hermanos and asks Jimmy to observe the restaurant. Their investigation brings Gus Fring into view. Jimmy and Kim hire Francesca to help manage their office. After learning about Chuck's recording through Ernesto, Jimmy confronts his brother in anger, destroys the tape and forces his way into the house. Witnesses are waiting. His emotional reaction gives Chuck a stronger route to attack his professional standing.

Jimmy faces criminal charges following the confrontation at Chuck's house. Kim joins his defence, but Chuck's main objective is a disciplinary outcome that could end Jimmy's legal career. The brothers' conflict becomes a formal legal battle. Mike meets Gus, who explains his interest in keeping Hector alive for the moment. Rather than ending Mike's campaign, Gus offers a way to redirect it. Both stories turn on deals whose full purposes are only gradually revealed.

Gus and Hector compete within the cartel's business structure, with Gus maintaining a controlled public image while managing dangerous rivals. Mike helps prepare Jimmy and Kim's defence by obtaining photographs inside Chuck's house. The damage from Jimmy's intrusion and the arrangement of Chuck's surroundings become strategically useful. Kim challenges assumptions about how the recording should be handled. The episode assembles the evidence and relationships that will matter at Jimmy's disciplinary hearing.

Jimmy's disciplinary hearing becomes a confrontation over credibility, family history and Chuck's claimed sensitivity to electricity. Kim questions the witnesses and develops the defence's account. Jimmy then reveals that a charged battery has been placed in Chuck's pocket without his noticing. The demonstration prompts an emotional outburst in which Chuck exposes his resentment and distrust of Jimmy. Jimmy avoids the outcome Chuck wanted, but the public victory deepens the personal damage between them.

Jimmy receives a one-year suspension and tries to recover the cost of television airtime he can no longer use to advertise legal services. He creates a new advertising business under the name Saul Goodman. Chuck struggles with the aftermath of the hearing. Nacho fears Hector's plan to involve his father's business and begins considering a way to remove the threat. Gus and Mike continue to develop their working relationship around shared practical interests.

Suspended from practising law, Jimmy juggles community service, advertising sales and mounting expenses. Selling television commercials proves much harder than persuading legal clients. Nacho seeks empty capsules as part of his plan against Hector, and Mike becomes involved reluctantly. Kim continues her demanding Mesa Verde work. When Jimmy asks his malpractice insurer for financial relief, he reveals damaging information about Chuck, creating consequences that extend beyond his own immediate money problems.

Jimmy pressures a music shop into compensating him after its owners refuse to pay for the commercial arrangement he expected. Kim takes on additional work and struggles to balance ambition with exhaustion. Chuck makes visible progress in managing daily life outside his house. Nacho prepares the capsule switch that could affect Hector's health, while Mike pursues a way to support his family financially. Small tactical successes coexist with mounting pressure across the characters' lives.

Jimmy manipulates Irene's friends to isolate her, hoping she will agree to settle the Sandpiper case and release his share of the fees. Chuck's insurance problems intensify his conflict with Howard and threaten his role at HHM. Kim pushes herself to complete another major assignment, then crashes her car. Nacho carries out his plan to replace Hector's medication. Each storyline shows a character pursuing a goal while underestimating the human consequences of the method.

Kim begins recovering from her accident and reconsiders her workload. Jimmy sees the harm he caused Irene and deliberately exposes his own manipulation so that her friendships can recover, sacrificing his elder-law reputation. Howard buys Chuck out of HHM after their dispute becomes untenable. Hector collapses during a confrontation, and Gus intervenes to keep him alive. Alone and increasingly distressed, Chuck dismantles his home searching for electricity before starting the fire that kills him.

Jimmy learns of Chuck's death and moves through the practical steps of mourning with little visible emotional release. Howard believes the insurance dispute and Chuck's forced departure from HHM contributed to the death. Jimmy lets him carry that burden. Mike tests security at a Madrigal warehouse while establishing a plausible cover for his paid role. Gus studies the circumstances of Hector's collapse, bringing Nacho's hidden actions under increasing scrutiny.

Jimmy impresses the owners of a copier business during an interview, then abruptly rejects their offer and criticizes their willingness to trust him. Kim confronts Howard over how he has handled Chuck's death and its effect on Jimmy. Mike insists on making his Madrigal security role operationally credible. Gus brings in a specialist for Hector and demonstrates his power over Nacho by killing Arturo. Nacho's attempt to escape one master leaves him controlled by another.

Jimmy arranges the theft of a valuable figurine from the copier office, treating it as an easy way to make money. Nacho takes part in a staged attack designed to explain Arturo's death and support Gus's deception. Kim observes court proceedings and becomes interested in people whose cases receive little attention. Gus considers the technical possibilities of a future methamphetamine operation. Chuck's letter to Jimmy produces a restrained response from him and a much more emotional one from Kim.

Jimmy finds work at a mobile-phone shop but discovers that having little to do does not suit him. Kim becomes increasingly drawn to public-defence cases while Mesa Verde continues its expansion. Mike challenges a support-group participant whose story he believes is false, unsettling Stacey. Nacho returns to the Salamanca operation under Gus's control. Across these stories, characters conceal distress behind professional routines, and their frustration emerges in choices that others find difficult to understand.

A flash-forward shows Saul and Francesca clearing his office as his world collapses. In the earlier timeline, Jimmy develops a business selling prepaid phones to people who value anonymity, but a group of teenagers robs him. Kim's growing commitment to criminal-defence work competes with her corporate responsibilities. Gus evaluates engineers for a secret underground construction project. Werner's realistic assessment earns the job, and Mike becomes responsible for keeping the crew's work secure and hidden.

Jimmy arranges a frightening lesson for the teenagers who robbed him, using Huell and another associate to regain control of his phone business. Kim negotiates a role at Schweikart & Cokely that supports Mesa Verde while leaving room for other cases. Howard admits that HHM is struggling, and Jimmy pushes him to recover. Mike organizes living and working conditions for Werner's construction crew, balancing security requirements with the realities of a long, isolating assignment.

A montage follows Jimmy and Kim as their daily routines become increasingly separate. Jimmy's prepaid-phone business grows, while Kim establishes herself at Schweikart & Cokely. When Huell strikes a police officer, Jimmy asks Kim to help prevent a prison sentence. Kim sees weaknesses in the prosecution but becomes interested in a more elaborate solution. Meanwhile, Werner's crew faces the strain of extended isolation, and Mike must contain the risks created by their frustration.

Jimmy and Kim stage a campaign of letters and telephone calls from Huell's supposed hometown supporters. The invented community pressure persuades the prosecutor to reconsider the case. Energized by the success, they collaborate on another deception to change Mesa Verde's approved building plans. At the construction site, Werner's homesickness becomes harder to manage. The episode brings Jimmy and Kim closer through shared manipulation while showing how apparently contained schemes can encourage larger risks.

Jimmy applies to regain his law licence but is rejected because the panel finds him insincere. His failure leads to an argument with Kim about support, responsibility and how others see him. Kim eventually agrees to help with an appeal. Mike discovers that Werner has escaped the secure construction site to meet his wife. The security breach creates an urgent search, while Lalo's arrival introduces a rival eager to understand Gus's hidden activities.

A flashback shows Jimmy celebrating his admission to the bar with Chuck. In the present, Jimmy and Kim build an appeal around the brothers' relationship, and Jimmy's emotional speech wins reinstatement. He then reveals his plan to practise as Saul Goodman. Mike tracks Werner down, but Gus decides the breach cannot be forgiven. Mike kills him after arranging for his wife to leave safely. Professional success and professional obedience both come at a severe personal cost.

Jimmy launches his Saul Goodman practice with an energetic promotion aimed at criminal clients. Kim is uncomfortable with some of his methods, yet uses a misleading story to persuade a client to accept a plea. Gus manages the cartel's suspicions about Werner and the construction project. In the Gene timeline, a taxi driver recognizes Saul, prompting him to contact the disappearer before deciding to handle the problem himself. Reinvention provides opportunity while leaving old dangers unresolved.

A discount promotion encourages two young clients to behave recklessly, and their escalating crimes bring them into Saul's orbit. Nacho remains trapped between the Salamancas and Gus, who wants him closer to Lalo. Kim struggles with the consequences of her own deceptive advice and the increasingly uncomfortable overlap between her values and Jimmy's methods. Mike's grief and anger lead him toward confrontation. Saul's growing practice creates demand by appealing directly to people others dismiss.

Nacho brings Saul to Lalo, who wants legal help for Krazy-8. Saul arranges a relationship with the DEA that serves a cartel strategy rather than simply his client's immediate interests. Kim faces Everett Acker, a homeowner resisting Mesa Verde's plan to remove him from his property. Her attempts to connect with him reveal how differently they understand her role. Mike continues to act recklessly, while Saul's legal work becomes more deeply entangled with organized crime.

Howard offers Jimmy a position at HHM, but Jimmy responds indirectly by damaging Howard's property with bowling balls. Kim develops a plan to help Acker resist Mesa Verde and involves Jimmy. Gus adjusts to the DEA's seizure of cartel money while preserving his position. Mike provokes another street confrontation and is seriously injured. The episode shows characters redirecting frustration into actions that complicate their lives rather than resolving the underlying conflict.

Mike recovers in a Mexican village connected to Gus and gradually understands more about his employer's history and motives. Kim and Jimmy use a succession of tactics to delay Acker's eviction and pressure Mesa Verde. Rich Schweikart begins to suspect that Kim is too personally involved in the dispute. What began as legal advocacy develops into a contest of persistence and deception, forcing Kim to decide how far she is willing to oppose her own client.

Kim tries to limit Jimmy's attack on Mesa Verde, but Saul surprises her at the settlement meeting with damaging advertisements and a dispute over the bank's logo image. The pressure produces a financial result for Acker while humiliating Kim professionally. Instead of ending the relationship, she proposes marriage as a way to change their legal exposure and expectations. Mike helps build the case that will put Lalo in custody, advancing Gus's strategy against the Salamancas.

Jimmy and Kim marry and agree on a new standard of honesty between them. Saul represents Lalo in a murder case, using information supplied through Mike to undermine the prosecution's evidence. The judge sets bail at seven million dollars. Gus and Nacho arrange an attack on a Los Pollos Hermanos restaurant to support the larger deception. Jimmy also lashes out at Howard, whose job offer touches unresolved feelings about Chuck, status and Jimmy's chosen identity.

Saul agrees to collect Lalo's seven-million-dollar bail in the desert for a substantial fee. Gunmen ambush him on the return journey, and Mike intervenes to save his life. With Saul's car disabled and another attacker still nearby, the two carry the money across the desert on foot. Exhaustion and a lack of water test Saul's endurance. Back in Albuquerque, Kim grows desperate for information and visits Lalo, exposing herself more directly to the danger surrounding Jimmy.

Jimmy returns with Lalo's bail money but hides the ambush from Lalo and initially conceals the truth from Kim. He struggles with the psychological aftermath of the desert. Kim leaves her corporate work to focus on helping people through pro bono defence. Suspicious about Jimmy's damaged car, Lalo returns to question him at home. Kim confronts Lalo's account and assumptions, helping Jimmy survive the encounter while Mike watches from a distance, prepared for violence.

Kim and Jimmy retreat to a hotel after Lalo's visit. Kim begins proposing a scheme against Howard that could accelerate the Sandpiper settlement and fund her public-interest work. Jimmy is unsettled by how seriously she means it. Nacho accompanies Lalo to Mexico and must assist Gus's planned assassination. The attack fails, and Lalo survives. Nacho escapes, but the failure leaves him exposed and turns the danger Jimmy and Kim hope is over into a continuing threat.

A sequence reveals the luxury and excess accumulated during Saul's later career. Earlier, Jimmy and Kim begin their campaign to damage Howard's reputation, planting the suggestion of drug use at his golf club. Nacho hides after the failed assassination and relies on instructions that may not protect him. Lalo conceals his survival while preparing his response. The season opens with carefully managed appearances, as several characters work from incomplete or deliberately false information.

Jimmy approaches the Kettlemans with a story about Howard's alleged drug use, helping spread the accusation. Kim then confronts the couple over their tax business and prevents them from exploiting the situation. Nacho realizes that his motel refuge is unsafe and escapes an attack. Gus considers how to control the fallout, while Mike resists a plan that could endanger Nacho's father. The parallel schemes show persuasion and coercion being used to make others carry the risk.

Nacho negotiates protection for his father and agrees to surrender himself under a plan that shields Gus. Before the cartel leaders, he gives the required account but also claims responsibility for Hector's stroke. He then kills himself rather than submit to their intended punishment. Mike witnesses the outcome from a distance. Meanwhile, Jimmy and Kim continue preparing their Howard scheme, including access to his car, unaware of how close their world is to the cartel's violence.

Jimmy disguises himself as Howard and stages a public confrontation with Wendy using Howard's car. Kim ensures that Cliff Main sees the scene while discussing an ambitious legal-aid project. She notices surveillance and confronts the men following her. Mike explains that Lalo is alive and that she and Jimmy are being watched for their protection. Saul's association with the Salamancas attracts new clients, encouraging him to consider the office that will define his later practice.

Howard challenges Jimmy to a boxing match, hoping to bring their conflict into the open, but also hires an investigator to follow him. Gus remains intensely alert to Lalo's possible return and prepares the unfinished laboratory for a confrontation. In Germany, Lalo visits Werner's widow while seeking information about the secret project. Kim and Jimmy continue assembling their scheme, even as Kim receives an opportunity to pursue meaningful legal work beyond the campaign against Howard.

Jimmy and Kim prepare photographs and a drugged encounter to sabotage the Sandpiper mediation. A detail about the mediator's appearance threatens the plan, and Kim abandons a professional opportunity to help repair it. A flashback shows an early lesson in deception from her mother. Lalo pursues another member of Werner's construction crew to uncover Gus's operation. The episode brings both plots close to execution while showing the alternatives the characters choose to leave behind.

Jimmy and Kim execute their plan against Howard during the Sandpiper mediation. Altered photographs and a drugged Howard make his accusations appear irrational, pushing the case toward settlement. Howard later confronts them at their apartment and describes the damage they have caused. Lalo arrives unexpectedly during the argument. Before Jimmy or Kim can understand or control the situation, he shoots Howard. Their elaborate manipulation collides with violence that has no place in the story they planned.

Lalo uses Jimmy and Kim to draw Mike's security team away from Gus. Kim is sent to kill Gus, but reaches his men instead. Gus recognizes the diversion and goes to the unfinished laboratory, where Lalo records evidence of the secret construction. Gus uses his preparation and familiarity with the site to kill him. Mike manages the aftermath and supplies Jimmy and Kim with a cover story. Howard and Lalo are buried beneath the laboratory together.

Jimmy and Kim try to live with the cover story after Howard's death. At his memorial, Kim reinforces the false account, then recognizes what their partnership has become. She quits the law and leaves Jimmy, admitting that she knew Lalo was alive. Gus preserves his cartel position, while Mike visits Nacho's father and finds that promises of justice cannot erase the loss. A later scene shows Jimmy fully inhabiting Saul's extravagant, emotionally insulated life.

Living as Gene, Jimmy befriends Marion to gain leverage over her son Jeff, who has recognized him as Saul. Rather than flee, Gene recruits Jeff into a carefully rehearsed department-store robbery. He distracts a security guard while Jeff steals selected goods. When a mishap threatens the timing, Gene improvises an emotional diversion. Afterward, he uses their shared criminal exposure to demand silence. The successful operation awakens skills and appetites that his quiet Omaha life had suppressed.

Flashbacks revisit Saul's first encounter with Walt and Jesse and Mike's warning about Walt's risks. In Omaha, Gene contacts Francesca and learns about the collapse of his former world. A call to Kim ends badly, and he turns toward a more predatory series of scams with Jeff and Buddy. They target wealthy men and steal financial information. Buddy refuses to rob a man with cancer, but Gene insists on continuing, revealing how far his need for control has overtaken restraint.

Kim lives a cautious, uneventful life in Florida until Gene's call pushes their buried history back into view. She returns to Albuquerque, submits an affidavit and tells Cheryl the truth about Howard. A flashback shows her final encounter with Saul and a conversation with Jesse outside his office. Gene completes the risky burglary, but Jeff is arrested. Marion becomes suspicious, discovers Gene's identity online and uses her emergency alert device to summon help as he confronts her.

After fleeing Marion's house, Gene is arrested. Saul uses negotiation and a carefully shaped story to obtain an extraordinarily favourable proposed sentence. Learning of Kim's confession changes the direction of his defence. At the hearing, he abandons the protective account and admits his role in Walt's criminal enterprise, along with the damage he caused Chuck. He accepts a much longer sentence and reclaims the name Jimmy McGill. Kim later visits him in prison, where they share a brief, quiet connection.
